deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to Grothendieck's 1953 notes on decreasing rearrangements, a draft of his Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955), 'Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace'. The previous page introduced the decreasing rearrangement φ_f of a positive measurable function f on a measure space M. It exists iff every set {f ≥ a}, a>0, has finite measure. It satisfies φ_f(t) = inf{ ||(1−1_E) f||_∞ : m(E) ≤ t } and comes with its 'spectral' measure μ (μ_f = −dφ_f, the distribution of f).

This page:
(i) Integrability of φ near 0. φ is integrable near 0 iff ∫_1^∞ dσ ∫_σ^∞ dμ(s) < ∞. By Fubini this is ∫_1^∞ (s−1) dμ(s) < ∞, i.e. condition (6): ∫^∞ s dμ(s) < ∞. For μ = μ_f this says f is integrable on {f ≥ 1}.
(ii) Definition (7): Φ_f(t) = ∫_0^t φ_f(s) ds. This is the Hardy–Littlewood maximal function of the rearrangement, i.e. the Ky Fan type norm. It is continuous, increasing and concave.
(iii) Definition (8): if log φ_f is integrable near 0 (equivalently log f integrable on {f ≥ 1}), set Ψ_f(t) = ∫_0^t log φ_f(s) ds. Ψ_f is finite everywhere iff the support of f has infinite measure. Otherwise Ψ_f = −∞ beyond t_0 = |{f ≠ 0}|.
(iv) Definition (9): Δ_f(t) = exp Ψ_{|f|}(t). This is a 'truncated geometric-mean determinant'. It vanishes beyond t_0 when t_0 is finite.
(v) The pointwise rearrangement inequalities (5) of the previous page are said to give corresponding inequalities for Φ, Ψ, Δ. The key ones are (10) Ψ_{fg} ≤ Ψ_f + Ψ_g, i.e. (11) Δ_{fg} ≤ Δ_f Δ_g. This is weak log-majorization of (fg)* by f* g*, the commutative analogue of the Weyl–Horn multiplicative inequality for singular values.

The next page sets Δ(f) = Δ_{|f|}(|M|) = exp ∫ log|f|. This is multiplicative, 'like a multiple of a determinant': the commutative Fuglede–Kadison determinant. Δ_{1+f}(t) is then built for finite measure. The whole programme is evidently a commutative model to be transported to semifinite von Neumann algebras with trace. There it would give generalized s-numbers and the truncated Fuglede–Kadison determinants Δ_t(T) = exp ∫_0^t log μ_s(T) ds, later systematized by Fack–Kosaki (1986).
errors: 'Supposons log φ_f sommable au voisinage de 0 (a fortiori φ_f le sera)': the implication is reversed. Integrability of φ_f near 0 implies integrability of log⁺ φ_f near 0, but not conversely. Example: φ(t) = 1/t has integrable log near 0 but is not integrable. Unless he means 'a fortiori' relative to the earlier hypothesis that Φ_f exists, the parenthesis is wrong.

Claim that Δ_f(t) is a continuous function of t is false at t_0 when t_0 = |{f ≠ 0}| is finite. Ψ_f(t_0) can be finite (e.g. f = 1_A with |A| = t_0 gives Δ_f(t_0) = 1), while Ψ_f(t) = −∞ for t > t_0. So Δ_f jumps from a positive value to 0. It is only upper semicontinuous / right-continuous in the appropriate sense.

The pointwise inequalities (5) from the previous page, φ_{f+g} ≤ φ_f + φ_g and φ_{fg} ≤ φ_f φ_g, are false pointwise. Counterexample: f = 1_A, g = 1_B with A, B disjoint of measure 1, evaluated at t = 1.5. Product counterexample: f = 2·1_A + 1_B, g = 1_A + 2·1_B, at t ∈ [1, 2). The correct pointwise forms are φ_{f+g}(s+t) ≤ φ_f(s) + φ_g(t) and φ_{fg}(s+t) ≤ φ_f(s) φ_g(t). Hence 'formulas (5) give the corresponding inequalities' is not a valid derivation as written. The integrated conclusions Φ_{f+g} ≤ Φ_f + Φ_g and (10)/(11) are nevertheless true (sub-/log-majorization).
'Cela est réalisé quand μ est borné' is unclear and not sufficient as stated. Condition (6) concerns the first moment of μ at infinity, not its total mass.

ideas.what: Decreasing rearrangement φ_f and its integral Φ_f(t) = ∫_0^t φ_f, used as a family of norms
ideas.modern_name: Non-increasing rearrangement f*, Hardy–Littlewood maximal function f**, Ky Fan norms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya (1929–34), G.G. Lorentz (1950); noncommutative version Grothendieck (1955), Fack–Kosaki (1986)
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955), Réarrangements de fonctions et inégalités de convexité dans les algèbres de von Neumann munies d'une trace

ideas.what: Truncated geometric-mean functional Δ_f(t) = exp ∫_0^t log φ_{|f|}(s) ds and its submultiplicativity Δ_{fg} ≤ Δ_f Δ_g
ideas.modern_name: Commutative case of the truncated Fuglede–Kadison determinant Δ_t; weak log-majorization (Weyl–Horn inequality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weyl (1949), Horn (1950) for matrices; Fuglede–Kadison (1952) for the determinant; Fack–Kosaki (1986) for Δ_t on τ-measurable operators
ideas.where_published: Possibly in Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955); unsure whether the truncated determinant is explicitly there

ideas.what: Δ(f) = exp ∫ log|f| as a multiplicative 'determinant' (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Fuglede–Kadison determinant in the abelian case (geometric mean)

missed.claim: Grothendieck in 1953 defines the t-truncated determinant Δ_f(t) = exp ∫_0^t log φ_f and states its submultiplicativity. This is the (commutative model of the) object Fack–Kosaki introduced in 1986 for τ-measurable operators. If exposé 113 did not include Δ_t, this is an unrecorded anticipation; if it did, it is merely a draft of it.
missed.quote: (9) Δ_f(t) = exp Ψ_{|f|}(t) ... Le plus important est (10) Ψ_{fg} ≤ Ψ_f + Ψ_g i.e. (11) Δ_{fg} ≤ Δ_f Δ_g
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit for generalized s-number / Fuglede–Kadison determinant inequalities in von Neumann algebras (used in L²-invariants, Brown measure, Haagerup–Schultz work), linking rearrangement theory directly to determinants in Grothendieck's own programme.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful draft of material largely published in Grothendieck's 1955 Bourbaki exposé. The explicit truncated determinant Δ_f(t) with Δ_{fg} ≤ Δ_f Δ_g is a nice anticipation of Fack–Kosaki's Δ_t, but it is in the commutative case and Grothendieck is already credited for generalized s-numbers. It contains minor errors.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: 'Cela est réalisé quand μ est borné, i.e.' — the following crossed-out line begins 'transcrite' / 'traduisible' rather than 'transitive'; it is uncertain.
'f étant sommable dans le complexe' likely reads 'f étant sommable dans le complémentaire [de f^{-1}([0,1[)]' or similar — uncertain.
(8) should read Ψ_f(t) = ∫_0^t log φ_f(s) ds; the integration variable is written as t in the manuscript.
